content: To write a manuscript effectively, it is essential to adhere to specific formatting principles that are widely accepted by editors and publishers. Below are detailed instructions for preparing a manuscript, written in clear and precise language: 1. Understand the Importance of Simplicity and Consistency Editors prefer manuscripts that are simple, familiar, and consistent in appearance. Avoid using flashy colors, unusual fonts, or other attention-grabbing elements, as these can detract from the content and frustrate the editor. Instead, aim for a clean and standardized format that allows the editor to focus on the substance of your work. 2. Follow Publisher-Specific Guidelines Before submitting your manuscript, check if the publisher has specific formatting requirements. These guidelines are often available on the publisher's website. 3. Acknowledge the Lack of a Universal Standard There is no single, universally accepted Standard Manuscript Format (SMF). Instead, there are general formatting principles with variations depending on the publisher or editor. If no specific instructions are given, choose a sensible and consistent format for your manuscript and stick to it throughout. 4. Basic Formatting Rules Use black text on white paper. Avoid using colored text or paper. For hard copy submissions, use high-quality, 20-pound bond white paper. Do not staple the pages; instead, package them securely for shipping. Choose a traditional, 12-point font such as Times New Roman, Courier, or Arial. Avoid decorative fonts like Comic Sans. Double-space the entire manuscript to enhance readability. Set one-inch margins on all sides of the page to allow space for editorial notes. Include a header on every page of the manuscript (except the title page). The header should contain your last name, the manuscript title (or an abbreviated version), and the page number, formatted as: Smith / My Manuscript / 23. Align the text to the left, leaving the right edge jagged. Do not justify the text. If submitting electronically, save the manuscript as a PDF unless instructed otherwise. 5. Title Page Layout The title page should include your full legal name (and pseudonym, if applicable), the manuscript's full title, your contact information, and the word count (precise or estimated). Place your legal name and contact information in the top left corner of the page. Place the word count in the top right corner. Use the exact word count if possible. Center the title halfway down the page in all capital letters. Below the title, write by and then your name or pseudonym as you wish it to appear. At the bottom of the page, you may include copyright information or your agent's contact details, if relevant. 6. Header Formatting The header should appear on every page of the manuscript except the title page. It should include your last name, the manuscript title (or an abbreviated version), and the page number. For example: Smith / My Manuscript / 1. Prefatory materials, such as a table of contents or acknowledgments, should use lowercase Roman numerals for page numbers (e.g., Smith / My Manuscript / iii). The main text begins with Arabic numeral 1. 7. Chapter Formatting Begin each chapter on a new page. Leave the top third of the page blank, except for the header. One-third of the way down the page, center the chapter number and title in all capital letters (e.g., CHAPTER 1 — THE BEGINNING). Start the text of the chapter four to six lines below the title. Do not indent the first paragraph of a chapter. Subsequent paragraphs should be indented consistently, either by five spaces or 0.5 inches (1.25 cm). 8. Ending the Manuscript Clearly indicate the end of the manuscript by centering the word END in all capital letters on the final page. For manuscripts with scenes (e.g., plays or screenplays), use a centered hashmark () to denote scene breaks. Footnotes are uncommon in non-academic manuscripts. Endnotes may be preferable if the notes consist solely of citations. 9. Using Google Docs for Formatting Set the page margins to one inch on all sides. This is the default setting in Google Docs, but you can adjust it by clicking File, selecting Page Setup, and entering 1 for all margins. Use left alignment for the text, which is the default in Google Docs. Change the line spacing to double by clicking the line spacing button and selecting Double from the drop-down menu. Select a 12-point font, preferably Times New Roman, unless otherwise specified. To create a header, click Insert, select Page Number, and choose the option that places the page number in the top right corner while excluding the title page. Add your last name and abbreviated title to the header. 10. Additional Tips Always review the submission guidelines provided by the agent or publisher. Academic manuscripts often require specific citation styles, such as MLA, APA, or Chicago. Verify the preferred style for your field. Proofread your manuscript thoroughly after using spellcheck. Consider reading it in reverse order or after a break to catch errors more effectively. 11. Warnings Avoid using unconventional formatting to make your manuscript stand out. Editors prefer standard formats and may reject manuscripts that deviate from them. Do not manipulate font size or spacing to alter the manuscript's length. Editors are experienced in identifying such tactics.
